Formulation
- Predisposing factors: History of osteoarthritis (previous GP diagnosis).
- Precipitating factors: Acute onset of left elbow swelling noticed approximately one week prior to consultation.
- Perpetuating factors: Not recorded.
- Protective factors: Generally fit, engages in regular exercise, no other active medical complaints reported.
- Summary: Patient presents with a one-week history of non-tender, slightly warm swelling at the tip of the left elbow consistent with clinician's provisional diagnosis of bursitis. No systemic symptoms or signs of septic arthritis observed during the consultation. Plan includes short course of anti-inflammatory therapy and blood tests to screen for inflammatory, infectious, rheumatologic causes and gout; follow-up arranged contingent on test results or sooner if worsening/red flags.

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Left elbow bursitis (provisional)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce elbow swelling and discomfort
  - Avoid progression or complications (infection)
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Reduce inflammation and monitor for infectious or systemic causes
  - Obtain diagnostic blood tests to exclude rheumatologic or infectious causes (including gout screen)
  - Reassess the joint following test results and symptom course
- Actions (Patient):
  - Take ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food as advised; stop if develops heartburn
  - Complete arranged blood tests when test forms are received
  - Contact clinic for follow-up after blood tests or sooner if symptoms worsen (increasing redness, spreading redness, increasing pain)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Send blood test forms to patient's home for inflammatory markers, rheumatology antibody screen, gout investigations, and infection markers (full screen as discussed)
  - Advise NSAID use (ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food) and provide safety advice (stop if heartburn)
  - Arrange follow-up appointment (phone/video or face-to-face based on patient preference) after blood test results or sooner if red flags
  - Provide clear instructions regarding emergency presentation for signs suggestive of septic arthritis

Secondary Problem: Osteoarthritis (history)
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Maintain joint function and manage symptoms as needed
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Continue conservative management and monitor for exacerbations
- Actions (Patient):
  - Continue regular physical activity as tolerated (patient reports running 2–3 times/week)
  - Report any new or worsening joint symptoms to GP
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Note history of osteoarthritis in medical record
  - Consider further management if symptoms exacerbate after assessment and investigations (not specified in this consult)

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered:
  - Explanation of likely bursitis (inflammation of fluid sac around joint)
  - Use of anti-inflammatory medication (ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily, take after food; stop if heartburn)
  - Need for blood tests to exclude other causes (inflammatory markers, rheumatologic antibodies, gout, infection)
  - Red flags prompting urgent review (increasing redness, intense pain, spreading redness) and that septic arthritis would require urgent assessment
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Increased pain
  - Increasing redness or spreading redness around the elbow
  - Rapid worsening of symptoms (seek urgent review)
- Coping Strategies:
  - Use of NSAID as advised
  - Seek earlier face-to-face assessment if visible worsening occurs
  - Follow-up after blood tests for review and further management
